chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Mithamī from Aban from Hakam ibn Hukeym from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding His Words, the Mighty and Majestic: 'And the adulteress, none shall marry her except an adulterer or an idolater.' He said: 'That is only regarding the open (blatant).' Then he said: 'If a person commits adultery, then repents, he may marry wherever he desires.'
ai.seo_question: Does repentance lift the marriage prohibition for an adulterer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the Quranic prohibition in Surah al-Nur applies specifically to those who commit adultery openly (al-jahr), distinguishing between public scandal and private sin. He further establishes that upon sincere repentance (tawbah), the restriction is lifted, allowing the repentant individual to marry anyone, including those not previously prohibited, highlighting the transformative power of repentance in Shia jurisprudence.
